producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 2:47PM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves along the coast. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.25 feet above ground
level is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas.

* WHERE...Grays Harbor County Coast zone.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST Saturday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 5 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected. Dangerous breaking waves can knock people
off their feet and sweep them into the ocean. Driftwood and
debris in powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the
beach observing the ocean. High surf will result in erosion to
beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads,
trails, and coastal structures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Everyone should remain out of the water and well back from the
surf zone. This includes staying off jetties, piers, and other
coastal structures. Never turn your back on the ocean and keep
children and pets close. Know the tides and forecast conditions.
Follow warning signs and respect barriers.

properties.areaDesc: Greater Lake Tahoe Area; Greater Lake Tahoe Area
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 13 at 1:32AM PST until November 14 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
* CHANGES...None.

* WHAT...Heavy wet snow. Snow accumulations near 12 inches above 7000
feet, with up to 6 inches below 7000 feet. Snow accumulations up to
20 inches along the crest west of Lake Tahoe. Wind gusts of 70 to
90 mph over ridges and gusts of 45 to 55 mph for Truckee and Lake
Tahoe communities. Wave heights 2 to 5 feet on Lake Tahoe.

* WHERE...Greater Lake Tahoe Area.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 10 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Friday evening commute. Strong winds and Sierra
cement snow could cause damage to trees and power lines. Strong
winds and rough waves on Lake Tahoe will create hazardous
conditions for small watercraft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A burst of heavy snow is likely with this
system late this afternoon into the evening with snow levels
falling to as low as 5500 feet.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 12 at 8:10PM EST by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Multiple rounds of showers, mostly rain in the valleys and snow at
higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night.
Temperatures should be cold enough for minor snow accumulations at
elevations above 2,500 feet with mainly a dusting to half inch on
grassy and elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow
accumulations are possible over the highest portions of Big Black
Mountain. The snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in
the 20s could yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of
Highway 160  near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on
Friday night.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.
